summary_paragraph: A 65-year-old male with a complex medical history including end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, coronary artery disease with prior CABG and stents, peripheral vascular disease, and type 2 diabetes was admitted for sudden-onset sub-sternal chest pain that occurred during a dialysis session. The pain was consistent with his known angina and resolved with nitroglycerin and morphine. Serial troponins remained stable without rise, and CK levels trended downward, indicating no acute myocardial infarction. EKG showed new T-wave flattening in leads V2-V5. The patient was observed for over 24 hours, remained pain-free, and completed dialysis. Management included continuation of cardiac medications, discontinuation of Nexium due to potential interaction with Plavix, and transition to ranitidine. He was discharged home with instructions to follow up promptly with his cardiologist, monitor weight daily, and continue wound care for a chronic leg ulcer. No stress testing was performed due to low likelihood of changing management.
problems: Coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery
